goal:
Implement issue #50: a delivery run that ended in needs_human must reconcile to
merged once the merge channel says its PR merged, without erasing anything.

Edit exactly two files. Use replace_in_file for both edits; do not rewrite
either file wholesale.

1) apps/code_review_pipeline/delivery/run_store.py

   (a) In _merge_target, this guard

           if target is None or current in _TERMINAL_RUN_STATES:
               return None

       must let exactly one terminal case through: current is
       DeliveryRunState.NEEDS_HUMAN and the merge state is MergeState.MERGED.
       Every other terminal current state still returns None. Keep the
       backward-order check and the unknown-state handling as they are.

   (b) In DeliveryRunStore.sync, this block

           if run.state in _TERMINAL_RUN_STATES:
               # A terminal run snapshot is immutable.  The merge channel keeps
               # the live record; a late/out-of-order poll must not overwrite it.
               return run

       must still freeze a terminal run except for that same fold. A late
       non-terminal record such as watching still changes nothing, and merged,
       rejected, failed and budget_exhausted are never rewritten by it.

   (c) Behaviour to keep:
       - when the resulting state equals the current state and run.merge equals
         record, sync still returns the run without saving and without writing
         audit;
       - run.failure keeps its exact value: the original infra_error stays;
       - the existing audit.record call keeps its action / merge_state / pr /
         merged_sha keys and gains detail key folded_from with the previous
         state value (needs_human) only when this call folds a terminal run.

2) tests/unit/test_delivery_store.py

   After test_sync_from_merge_never_reopens_terminal_run, add two tests:
   - a needs_human run carrying FailureInfo(FailureCode.INFRA_ERROR, boom)
     whose merge record is merged advances to MERGED, keeps that same failure
     object, and the audit detail reports folded_from needs_human. Capture
     audit the way test_audit_adapter_writes_transition_fields does: monkeypatch
     apps.code_review_pipeline.delivery.audit.record_audit, then pass
     WalDeliveryAudit() as audit= to sync.
   - one parametrized test over rejected, failed and budget_exhausted: the run
     comes back unchanged when the merge record says merged.
   Helpers already in the file: _run(state), _pushed_run(state), and
   _merge_record(state=MergeState.MERGED.value, merged_sha=c * 40).

Do not modify any other file.

Implement issue #67: the read_file truncation hint must tell the model how
much of the file it has not seen yet, so it can decide whether paging again
is worth the observation budget.

Edit exactly two files.

1) app/agents/workspace_tools.py

   In read_file, the truncation hint currently reads:

   (truncated: returned N lines; continue with offset=M)

   Change it to carry the full pagination facts:

   (truncated: returned N lines of T total, T-M lines remain;
   continue with offset=M)

   where T is the total line count of the file and M is the next offset
   (last + 1, same value as today). Count the total only when a truncation
   actually happened - an untruncated return must stay byte-identical to
   today and must not scan the file a second time. The single-line-exceeds-
   read-bytes case (where picked holds one clipped line and last is that
   line number) gets the same total-lines treatment.

2) tests/unit/test_bench_tools.py

   Update the assertions that match the old hint text to the new one, and
   add assertions that the hint includes the total line count and the
   remaining line count for at least one multi-page case and the single
   oversized-line case. Keep every existing untruncated-return assertion
   unchanged.

Do not modify any other file. Do not change ToolLimits, the line numbering
format (4-space right-aligned line number, pipe separator), or the
offset-past-EOF message.

changed files - when the change includes test files that the verify command
never references, that mismatch must be visible at prepare time, not only
at the human push-approval gate.

delivery (delivery tests) while the change touched bench tool tests; the
verify exited 0 without ever running the changed tests. The mismatch was
caught by the human at the approval gate, costing one full implementation
budget. Today nothing in the tool layer signals it.

Step 1. Read apps/code_review_pipeline/change/pipeline.py once (limit 600)
and apps/code_review_pipeline/delivery/flow.py once (limit 500). Two reads
total. Do not read anything else yet.

Step 2. Immediately make the pipeline.py and flow.py edits described below,
using replace_in_file. Do not read any other file before both edits exist.

Step 3. For each test file: read the first 40 lines (imports and fixtures)
and the last 60 lines only. The test files are large (1426 and 798 lines);
you do NOT need their middles. Append the new tests at the end of each file.
The test files contain no _GitHub helper - if your new test needs a GitHub
stub, define a small class _GitHub inside the test function itself. Do not
search the file for helpers you can define yourself in three lines.

Step 4. Run the verification once and fix failures if any.

Never read a file twice; each read stays in your context. Total reads must
stay under 10. More than half your steps must be edits and verification.

The change, in detail. Edit exactly four files.

1) apps/code_review_pipeline/change/pipeline.py

   In prepare_bundle, in the VERIFIED branch (after bundle.files is known
   non-empty), add a coverage check:

   - Test files among bundle.files: a path containing tests/ or a basename
     starting with test_.
   - If there are no test files among the changes, skip the check entirely
     (source-only or docs-only changes must not be flagged).
   - Otherwise, extract path tokens from self._verify_command by splitting
     on whitespace and stripping surrounding quotes. A token covers a test

     token.rstrip(slash) + slash, or the token is . or ./ or tests or

2) apps/code_review_pipeline/delivery/flow.py

3) tests/unit/test_change_pipeline.py

   warning and verify_covers_changes True; a source-only change produces

   Reuse the existing fixtures and helpers of this test module; do not

4) tests/unit/test_delivery_flow.py

   Assert that the READY_FOR_PUSH_APPROVAL audit detail carries the

Implement issue #77: the tool loop never shows the model its remaining
budget, and it never marks repeated reads. The loop tracks executed steps
and cumulative tokens internally, but those facts never reach the model
messages; the static Budget line in the first user message is the only
signal. Ledger row 10 evidence: 15 starts for one delivery, 10 of them died
paging through files - dlv-dfba8210 spent 123 read_file and 63 search calls
of 200 steps (93 percent), including exact repeats of the same read and
eight consecutive searches with the same pattern; dlv-0e9f6389 finished all
edits and still read until the 3.5M token cap.

Work order - follow it strictly, in this sequence:

Step 1. Read app/agents/memory.py once (limit 200) and app/agents/stubs.py
offset 180 limit 250 once (the execute_tool_loop function). Two reads total.
Do not read anything else yet.

Step 2. Immediately make the edits described below. Do not read any other
file before both source edits exist.

Step 3. For each test file: read the first 60 lines and the last 40 lines
only, then append the new tests at the end. Do not read the middles.

Step 4. Run the verification at most TWICE, fix what you can between the
two runs, then STOP calling tools and summarize your change. Do not chase
a fully green run: the governed pipeline re-runs the verification itself
after you finish, so your job is the change plus an honest summary, not a
perfect local record. Attempts 7 and 8 burned 65 verification cycles each
chasing green - do not repeat that.

Never read a file twice. Total reads must stay under 10.

API fact for your tests: the keyword argument that carries the policy into
execute_tool_loop is named memory_policy, not policy - write
memory_policy=MemoryPolicy(...) in tests. A previous attempt failed the
verify gate only on this wrong kwarg name (2 of 14 tests).

The change, in detail. Edit exactly four files.

1) app/agents/memory.py

   MemoryPolicy is a frozen dataclass with two fields today. Add:

   - budget_nudge_ratio: float = 0.75 - the usage ratio at which the
     per-observation budget line turns into a strong warning.
   - mark_repeated_reads: bool = True - master switch for the repeat marker.

   Docstring comments in the style of the existing fields. Nothing else in
   this file changes.

2) app/agents/stubs.py

   In execute_tool_loop, the model-facing copy of each observation is
   model_observation, produced by truncate_observation and appended as the
   tool message. The full observation stored in steps must stay byte-
   identical to today. Two additions, both applied to model_observation
   only, after truncation:

   a) Repeat marker. Track exact repeats while policy.mark_repeated_reads
      is true and the tool is read_file or search. The key is the tool name
      plus the parsed arguments: for read_file the tuple of path, offset,
      limit values as given; for search the tuple of path and pattern.
      Count every call of the same key. When the count is 2 or more,
      prepend one line to model_observation:

      [repeat #N of this exact call - the content is already in your
      context; do not read it again]

      where N is the occurrence count. Increment slot loop_repeat_marks by
      one per marked call. Paging (same file, different offset) is NOT a
      repeat and must not be marked. If arguments failed to parse as JSON,
      skip the marker. Do not block, reject or alter the tool result.

   b) Budget line. Append one line to the end of every model_observation:

      [cycle X/Y - tokens A/B - P percent used]

      where X is executed tool calls after this one, Y is max_steps, A is
      usage.total_tokens, B is max_tokens, P is the integer percentage
      A*100//B. When max_tokens is 0 or unset, use [cycle X/Y] only. When
      max_tokens is positive and the ratio is at or above
      policy.budget_nudge_ratio, append after the line: Budget running
      low: stop reading, move to editing and verification now.

   Also add slot counters: slot loop_budget_nudges increments once per
   model_observation that carries the strong-warning text. No other
   behavior changes: the step and token termination checks, the
   compaction, and the truncation all stay exactly as today.

3) tests/unit/test_structured_tool_loop.py

   Append tests reusing the existing fakes and helpers of this module:

   - a normal-budget run shows the cycle line with the right numbers in the
     tool message content, and the corresponding step observation in the
     result has NO cycle line (byte-identical evidence);
   - with a tiny max_tokens that pushes usage over budget_nudge_ratio, the
     strong-warning sentence appears and slot loop_budget_nudges increments;
   - a second identical read_file call gets the repeat marker with #2 and
     slot loop_repeat_marks is 1, while a read with a different offset does
     not get the marker;
   - with policy.mark_repeated_reads False no marker appears;
   - with max_tokens 0 the cycle line carries no token part.

   Do not change existing tests.

4) tests/unit/test_bench_memory.py

   Assert the two new MemoryPolicy defaults: budget_nudge_ratio 0.75 and
   mark_repeated_reads True. Do not change existing tests.

Do not modify any other file. Do not change ToolLoopStep, ToolLoopResult,
the termination conditions, or the compaction.

Implement issue #43: add a manual Docker build trigger to CI without cutting a release tag.

Edit exactly two files.

1) .github/workflows/ci.yml
   a) In the existing on: block add a workflow_dispatch trigger with one boolean input:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          run_docker:
            description: Build the Docker image without pushing (no release tag)
            type: boolean
            default: false
   b) Replace the if: line of the docker job with:
      if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.run_docker == 'true')
   c) Add this line to the Log in to ghcr.io step:
      if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
   d) In the Build and push step change only the push value to:
      push: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') }}

   Keep every other part of the paragraph unchanged, including the backticked token in the new clause.

Implement issue #62: the preflight report must land in the audit detail of
every delivery run that runs a preflight, both when it blocks and when it
passes, so a reviewer can see later what the run saw at start.

Edit exactly two files.

1) apps/code_review_pipeline/delivery/flow.py

   In run(), the preflight block (the code under if self._github is not
   None) currently has two paths:

   a) blocked path: the audit record with action preflight_blocked already
      exists. Add one key to its detail dict: preflight, holding
      report.to_dict(). Do not add a second audit entry.

   b) passing path: today the flow calls self._move(run, IMPLEMENTING,
      start). _move writes a detail dict with one action key and takes no extra
      keys. Extend _move with one optional keyword parameter, extra
      (default None); when provided, its items are merged into the audit
      detail after the action key. Then pass extra with one key preflight holding
      report.to_dict() from the preflight block on the passing path. Every
      existing _move caller stays unchanged, so existing audit sequences
      are untouched.

2) tests/unit/test_delivery_flow.py

   FakeAudit.record currently stores only the transition pair. Extend it to
   also keep the detail dicts (add a self.details list or store tuples of
   (previous, current, detail) alongside the existing transitions list -
   keep the existing transitions attribute working, other tests assert on
   it). Then:

   - in test_blocked_preflight_terminates_before_any_implementer_attempt,
     additionally assert the preflight_blocked audit entry detail carries
     the preflight key and that its checks include one named push with
     status blocked;
   - in test_passing_preflight_leaves_the_flow_unchanged, additionally
     assert the preparing-implementing transition detail carries the
     preflight key, and that a flow without github still produces detail
     with only the action key on that transition (the existing happy-path
     test already asserts the sequence; add the detail assertion there or
     in a small new test, your choice).

Do not modify any other file. Do not change the run-record schema, add
configuration, or alter the existing transitions attribute semantics.
